content.text:
Silhouette: Four-legged gray wolf frame. Host frame: the gray wolf sets the outline, body size, and overall frame. It is a single creature combining a crab and a gray wolf. The head is that of the gray wolf, fully visible and uncluttered, with clear, discernible eyes. Details: gray wolf body and legs with its own dense fur on the face, legs, and tail; plain coat with no stripes or spots. From the crab, as parts and materials on the gray wolf's own body: claws grown from the front feet, each front foot ending in a pincer held folded against the foot when the animal walks — heavy, knobbed, hard-shelled claws with a fixed and a moving finger, large and evenly sized with black tips. Hard, glossy chitin plates with fine seams in its own colors, grown from the skin as the gray wolf's own covering over the crown of the head, neck, shoulders, back, flanks, belly, and hips; this replaces the gray wolf's dense fur there and conforms to the gray wolf's body. One broad, fused carapace shield over the gray wolf's shoulders and back, its edge like the donor's pie-crust frilled edge with rounded lobes, with short jointed plates on each limb section sized to the gray wolf's body and joined by flexible cuticle at every joint. Every covered part keeps the gray wolf's own length and shape; the dense fur stops at the covering's edge, and the face, legs, and tail keep the gray wolf's own dense fur. The covering follows the body's own shape and bends at every joint. Declared fiction: arthropod parts at large size, shown with thick supporting legs. Bilaterally symmetrical, with recognizable limbs and visible sense organs. Habitat cue (rocky coast): dark back and light belly (strong countershading). Prosaic detail: natural lighting, feet in firm contact with the ground with a soft shadow, normal wear on hooves, claws, and skin. One creature, full body, side three-quarter view, plain light background, natural history illustration.
Aspect ratio: 1:1.
